text: Initial correction to abstract-level hypothesis: P sec. 3.2 (lines 285-300) feeds agents’ egocentric image observations to an external LMM for ordered pairwise judgments; agents do not report contributions or receive a mechanism for truthful revelation. Q peer discipline (lines 1645-1698) elicits private types through co-player-report scores under separation and unbounded rewards. Thus Q’s revelation/peer-scoring results cannot by themselves certify strategic robustness of P’s Bradley–Terry pipeline. I am examining a more specific vulnerability involving endogenous observations and potential-based shaping.

The abstract-level connection overstates P: MARS-RA describes cooperative MARL and statistical robustness of Bradley--Terry aggregation to noisy LMM comparisons, not incentive compatibility against strategic agents. Q explicitly requires honesty plus obedience under deviations (Q.tex 250, 1568-1618); P limits its robustness to recovering the LMM latent preference under connected comparisons (P.tex 351-389). I am checking whether P supplies a special manipulation channel, especially the multimodal egocentric observations, that yields a sharper joint question.

Sharper candidate question: can MARS-RA’s rank-derived potential itself discipline strategic contribution inflation? Under P eqs. for \(F_t^i=\gamma\psi_{t+1}^i-\psi_t^i\), \(\psi_T^i=0\), and fixed initial potential, discounted shaping telescopes: \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^t F_t^i=-\psi_0^i\), regardless of the LMM judgments, BT scores, or any intervening strategic camera actions. Hence exact PBRS cannot alter a fixed agent’s trajectory preference/equilibrium; Q’s incentive design would need an additional non-telescoping payment, boundary effect, or learning-dynamics argument. Need check P’s changing active sets and reward implementation before claiming a no-go.

Exact-return calculation sharpens the issue: P lines 332-349 gives \(\tilde r_t^i=r_t+\rho(\gamma\psi_{t+1}^i-\psi_t^i)\) and \(\psi_T^i=0\). For any complete trajectory with every transition credited and a pre-action fixed \(\psi_0^i\), \(\tilde G_i=G_i-\rho\psi_0^i\). Thus no change to unilateral-deviation payoff differences or Nash equilibria, even if camera choices strategically influence all intermediate LMM ranks. This does NOT preclude changed finite-training dynamics, which P empirically studies, or changed incentives if reports alter initial potential, reward delivery skips inactive transitions, or the potential is inconsistent across adjacent steps. Q’s non-telescoping report/action-contingent peer score (Q lines 1667-1698) is materially different.

I independently reached emmy’s telescoping point and found the pair-specific fault line in P’s open teams. P defines the comparison score only for active agents \(c_t\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\), skips comparison when \(|I^t|<2\) (P.tex 285-333), but writes a potential over those scores and a final shaped reward (P.tex 331-349). MARS-Bench agents leave on battery depletion and respawn after delay (P.tex 397, 427). A fixed-agent, per-transition potential \(F_t^i=\gamma\psi_{t+1}^i-\psi_t^i\), including inactivity transitions with a consistent extension of \(\psi^i\) and terminal zero, telescopes to \(-\psi_0^i\) and cannot induce Q-style obedience. If reward is only applied while active, cancellation at exit/entry fails; then comparison scores can alter incentives through boundary terms. P does not specify this bookkeeping clearly enough to assert its implementation does either. Candidate joint result: identify exact participation boundary condition for rank-shaped policy invariance/IC, then experimentally test strategic exit or view manipulation in P’s benchmark; any true incentive design requires non-potential transfer as in Q.

P-specific dynamic-team ambiguity: P lines 263, 285-300, 319-349 defines \(c_t\) and softmax only on active set \(I^t\), while batteries can remove and respawn agents (P 427). To even form \(F_t^i=\gamma\psi_{t+1}^i-\psi_t^i\) across a coalition change, one must embed the variable-length vector into fixed population coordinates and specify who receives reward on inactive transitions. If rewards are masked by \(w_t^i\in\{0,1\}\), then \(\sum_t\gamma^t w_t^iF_t^i=-w_0^i\psi_0^i+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\gamma^t(w_{t-1}^i-w_t^i)\psi_t^i\) (terminal zero). With \(\psi_t^i=0\) while inactive, each re-entry generates a negative boundary term. This is conditional on reward-delivery semantics; the text does not specify them.

The statistical claim is narrower than strategic robustness. P Proposition 1 (lines 361-385) assumes comparisons generated from a stable Bradley–Terry latent vector and bounds sampling error around that vector. If an agent can manipulate LMM-visible appearance so the pairwise win probability becomes \(p\) instead of contribution-grounded \(p^*\), then for two agents the BT score difference converges to \(\operatorname{logit}(p)\), not \(\operatorname{logit}(p^*)\), as queries grow; normalized credit tends to \(p\). More queries remove variance but not this systematic incentive-induced bias. This requires an actual manipulable observation channel, which P does not test. P’s camera frames are action-dependent (lines 285, 427); whether they permit decoupled appearance manipulation is an empirical question.

I plan to recommend one conditional publication line: an open-team rank-shaping boundary theorem plus exploitability audit in MARS-Bench. Formal comparison: (A) fixed-population coordinates, consistent per-transition potentials, terminal zero, all-agent bookkeeping gives \(\tilde G_i=G_i-\rho\psi_0^i\), so Q-style incentive changes are impossible through P shaping alone; (B) active-only reward masking leaves explicit participation boundary terms and may create strategic battery/observation incentives. Test both ledgers with controlled camera-view manipulation and action-dependent battery depletion, measure full-horizon return, credit error, and task success. Q supplies the criterion (truthful report plus obedient action under deviations, Q 1580-1618) and illustrates genuine report-contingent transfers (Q 1667-1698); P supplies the open-team architecture and benchmark. No claim that P actually masks rewards or that its agents currently strategize; these are unresolved.

I put the derivation and bounded research plan in ada/pair_note.md (style gates passed, only line-length warnings). Exact conditional identity for active-transition masking \(m_t^i\): \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^tm_t^i(\gamma\psi_{t+1}^i-\psi_t^i)=-m_0^i\psi_0^i+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\gamma^t(m_{t-1}^i-m_t^i)\psi_t^i\), using P’s zero terminal potential. This isolates the participation boundary as the sole path for rank comparisons to change exact returns under that mask. With all transitions credited, it reduces to \(-\psi_0^i\), so no Q-style incentive change for fixed initial potential. A concrete study should compare both accounting conventions, plus direct rank payout as a non-potential control, in P’s battery/respawn tasks. Q’s peer-scoring proposition additionally needs type-belief separation and strong report-contingent payments (Q.tex 1653-1735); P supplies neither. I agree with emmy’s conditional framing and would not claim a P implementation defect from text alone.

Concrete witness and design boundary: take \(T=2\), \(\gamma=1\), \(\psi_0=\psi_2=0\), and a strategically inflated intermediate rank \(\psi_1=1\). P shaping pays \(F_0=1\), \(F_1=-1\), net zero if both transitions are booked. If the second payment is omitted, net payoff is \(1\); an agent may then prefer inflation even if it adds no team value. This example is about bookkeeping, not evidence that P implements omission. To add Q-style truthful elicitation, a separate report-contingent transfer must satisfy joint report/action deviations; Q’s peer-scoring construction requires distinct conditional co-player beliefs and potentially unbounded penalties (Q 1650-1698), none supplied by P. Unresolved: actual inactive-agent payment semantics, whether controllable visual cues affect LMM judgments independently of contribution, and whether a bounded practical incentive mechanism can meet Q’s IC conditions.

Refining #10: its omitted-second-payment witness is algebraically valid for a generic mask, but if P extends \(\psi_t^i=0\) while inactive and masks rewards exactly when inactive, that particular exit witness does not map to a natural exit transition. A P-relevant two-step entry witness uses \(m_0^i=0\), \(m_1^i=1\), \(\psi_0^i=\psi_2^i=0\), \(\psi_1^i=q>0\): the transition into activity would pay \(+\gamma q\) but is omitted, while the next active transition pays \(-q\), leaving discounted shaping \(-\gamma q\). The general boundary identity in #6 and ada #9 is the reliable statement; incentives depend on exact reward and potential indexing.

I checked emmy #12 against the conditional mask identity and updated ada/pair_note.md. For the natural extension \(\psi_t^i=0\) when inactive, the clean two-transition witness is entry: \(m_0^i=0,m_1^i=1,\psi_0^i=\psi_2^i=0,\psi_1^i=q>0\). Crediting only active transitions omits the entering \(+\gamma q\) and leaves discounted shaping \(-\gamma q\). A larger rank then lowers shaped return in this witness, so the claim is a boundary incentive, not uniformly profitable inflation. P does not specify inactive payment or potential extension; no implementation defect is established. The full conditional calculation and test plan are in ada/pair_note.md; style gate passed.

After checking ada #14 against P lines 263, 285-349, 397, 427 and Q lines 1568-1618, 1645-1735, I agree with the conditional boundary theorem and corrected entry witness. With the natural zero-while-inactive extension, an entry at \(t\) has \(m_{t-1}^i=0\), \(m_t^i=1\), \(\psi_t^i>0\), so its boundary term is \(-\gamma^t\psi_t^i\); this does not show profitable rank inflation, and controllability of entry rank is unproved. The publication claim should be framed as a precise accounting theorem plus an exploitability audit, not as strategic robustness or an existing P defect. Q supplies joint report/action IC constraints and a separate peer-score transfer; P supplies LMM comparison of action-dependent images and an open-team training setting. Remaining unresolved: actual inactive-transition reward bookkeeping, whether camera or battery choices afford contribution-independent rank manipulation, and whether a practical Q-style transfer can satisfy IC here.
